q: What's the catch with that? What could I be getting wrong?
answer:
Short answer: the headline product-level recommendations are fragile — almost half the product-ad spend (₹1,44,857 of ₹1,68,844, 46.2%) is unallocated to any product, so the product ROAS rankings ignore a huge chunk of spend and can mislead which products truly drove returns. This data is by order date.

What to watch (biggest catches)
- Unallocated spend is huge: ₹1,44,857 (46.2% of the ₹1,68,844 product-ad portfolio). The unallocated row has no attributed orders, so you cannot tell from these product rows whether that spend helped the winners you’d scale.
- Small-sample volatility: many top-ROAS products have very low spend, so their performance is an “early signal” not a proven scale winner. Examples: Pawveralls Suspender Boots — spend ₹4,660, net ROAS ~3.8x, net profit ₹13,169; TangleGuard Leash — spend ₹2,699, net ROAS ~3.6x, net profit ₹7,016; Pet Pocket Hoodie — spend ₹1,575, net ROAS ~2.6x, net profit ₹2,597.
- Profit vs ROAS and loss pockets: ROAS>1 doesn't always mean a big dollar profit at scale. Some high-spend items are loss-making: WildTrail Boots — spend ₹13,331, net ROAS 0.7x, net profit −₹4,363. Also, the top 3 spenders (Pawveralls Pro Suspender Boots, WildTrail Boots, Sofa Seat Cover) concentrate ~23.7% of spend — risk of single-product exposure.
- Attribution & timing limits: this is an allocated, order-date view. Allocation model assumptions and later returns/cancels (finance/event-date) can change the true P&L; check P&L lines before large-scale budget moves.

Worth checking:
- Break down the unallocated spend by campaign and ad platform (to see where that ₹1,44,857 is coming from).
- Require a minimum spend or order threshold (e.g., test scale only after X days or Y orders) before increasing budgets on “early signal” products.

Period: 2026-10-22 to 2026-10-28 · Currency: INR · Data as of 2026-10-28
